version.changelog:
Initial release of docx-pdf-knowledge-parser.

- Parses local `.docx` and `.pdf` files into structured, report-first knowledge artifacts.
- Supports batch extraction, generating `ingest-report.md`, `kb-items.jsonl`, `failed-items.jsonl`, and `MEMORY.candidate.md`.
- Clearly routes files as parseable, for manual review, or failed, with detailed logging of failures.
- Does not write to `MEMORY.md` directly—focuses on reviewable, auditable outputs.
- Includes helper scripts and sample outputs for local testing and integration.

llm.summary: The skill's code, instructions, and requirements align with its stated purpose of locally parsing .docx and .pdf files into report-first outputs; there are no signs of hidden network exfiltration or unrelated credential requests.

dimensions.detail: The name/description match the included code and SKILL.md: the package parses local .docx and .pdf files and writes report artifacts. Declared resource needs are minimal (no env vars, no special binaries). The README and agents/openai.yaml mention a future Feishu connector, but there is no Feishu network or credential code in this release — this is a plausible 'skeleton' state rather than an incoherence.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md limits processing to files already available locally / provided to the runtime. The included run.py follows that workflow (requires --input-dir and --output-dir), uses only local filesystem reads and local output files, and does not attempt to read other system config, environment variables, or call external endpoints.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec in the registry (instruction-only), which is lower risk. The repo includes a requirements.txt listing python-docx and pypdf (standard PyPI libs). This is reasonable for the stated task, but the package dependencies will need to be installed by the host environment; there is no bundled arbitrary download or exotic installer.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requests no environment variables or credentials. The code contains placeholders (e.g., 'source_token' fields) and README/metadata mention Feishu integration in future, but current files do not access external credentials or services.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not always-enabled, is user-invocable, and does not modify other skills or system-wide settings. It only reads input directories and writes its own output files; no persistent agent-level privileges are requested.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to be a local parser/skeleton and is internally consistent. Before installing or running: (1) inspect and install the Python dependencies (python-docx, pypdf) in an isolated environment; (2) only point the tool at directories containing files you are comfortable having written to disk in plain text (MEMORY.candidate.md, kb-items.jsonl may contain extracted content); (3) note the repo advertises future Feishu integration but this release contains no network or credential code — if a later version adds connectors, re-audit for credential access and external endpoints; (4) scanned/image PDFs are not OCR'd by pypdf — they will be marked failed; run on non-sensitive samples first to verify behavior.
